findings.title: Malformed server-sent type string crashes process in getCassandraLongType
findings.claim: splitJavaCompositeTypes' result is indexed without a length check (names[1] for VectorType, make([]UDTField, len(names)-2) for UserType); a peer-supplied malformed type name causes an index-out-of-range or makeslice len-out-of-range panic. parseFrame's recover re-panics runtime.Error, killing the read goroutine and the process.

findings.title: nil SubType still panics at zero dimensions when destination is *any
findings.claim: The bound is skipped at Dimensions == 0 so a nil SubType cannot panic there, and a test asserts this, but the generic path then calls info.Zero(), which dereferences v.SubType unconditionally, so unmarshalVector(VectorType{}, nil, new(any)) still nil-derefs on Scan's goroutine.

findings.title: Degrade paths for map-arity and vector dimension-parse failures lose the type name
findings.claim: Only the unknown-basic-type branch keeps the name; map-arity failure and vector dimension-parse failure return NewNativeType(protoVer, TypeCustom) with no name, and the VectorType branch uses the bare prefix, so the nested-vector case still reports custom(org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.VectorType) with neither element type nor dimension.

findings.title: Saturation guard in vectorElemMinSize has no test coverage
findings.claim: Coverage profile reports zero executions for the saturation guard at marshal.go:1136-1138; existing tests cover fixed, variable-length, zero and negative rows but nothing large enough to trigger saturation.

findings.title: Allocation assertion measures process-global TotalAlloc rather than a scoped measurement
findings.claim: The test's allocation assertion measures process-global TotalAlloc; it caught the prior regression and never flaked, so tightening it is deferred as not worth doing now.

findings.title: readTypeInfo slices a vector custom-type string without bounds checking
findings.claim: readTypeInfo slices a vector custom-type string blind; inputs like ...VectorType, ...VectorTypeX, ...VectorType(...FloatType) all panic through parseFrame.

findings.title: readBytes trusts peer-supplied element length, causing slice-bounds panic
findings.claim: readBytes trusts the peer's element length, causing a slice-bounds panic in unmarshalUDT/unmarshalTuple on Scan's goroutine.

findings.title: Passing nil to skip a tuple column silently drops all later columns
findings.claim: Passing nil to skip a tuple column returns 1 instead of len(Elems), silently dropping every later column; Scan still returns true with nil error.

findings.title: vectorSliceReuse aliases one backing array across rows for float/double vectors
findings.claim: vectorSliceReuse aliases one backing array across rows for vector<float> and vector<double> only (introduced in commit f42df61).

findings.title: unmarshalTuple panics instead of erroring on mismatched or unexported destination field
findings.claim: unmarshalTuple panics instead of returning an error on a mismatched or unexported destination field.

findings.title: Element-failure error message always reports []uint8 regardless of actual payload type
findings.claim: The element-failure message uses %T on the payload, so it always says []uint8 regardless of the actual type.

findings.title: parseFrame's recover policy re-panics runtime.Error by design
findings.claim: parseFrame's recover policy of re-panicking runtime.Error is deliberate, not a defect.

findings.title: New bound in vector parsing cannot reject a well-formed payload
findings.claim: The new bound was checked and cannot reject a well-formed payload, verified via a round-trip test over 22 element types times 5 dimensions with clean results.

findings.title: nil SubType panic with Dimensions > 0 is pre-existing, not introduced by this change
findings.claim: nil SubType with Dimensions > 0 panicked identically at base, so the new bound neither introduces nor widens this panic.

findings.title: getCassandraLongType has a standing TODO for missing unit test coverage
findings.claim: getCassandraLongType has a // TODO: Cover with unit tests. comment at helpers.go:204 that still stands, flagged as a before-merge follow-up.

findings.title: No FuzzUnmarshal target exists for the unmarshal codepaths
findings.claim: Adding a FuzzUnmarshal target is suggested as a nice-to-have follow-up.
